# Current File is a native tree view: records whose links name the file (ADRs and decisions first),…

Current File is a native tree view: records whose links name the file (ADRs and decisions first), the Agent Change Graph's rows for it, and the document sections read from it; refreshed on editor change and save

A tree view, not a webview (VS Code's native-first guideline): three groups, each item opening the record, the review queue, or the new panel's Docs. With it, a gate approval now needs every version of its record to be the user's and status done (second automated security review: an agent could have edited a user's record into an approval).

---
Correction (2026-11-19): the gate-security claim above is now the opposite of what the code does. The user-only rule (ADR 10584 on #197) was dropped on 2026-11-12 ("the user's choice ... replacing #197's user-only approval"): to-spec now has the agent write the spec and record each gate itself, and `taskPage` in `vscode/app/model.js` counts a gate as passed by any decision record with `links.gate` and `status: "done"`, whoever wrote it — there is no `actor_kind` check any more. The rest still holds against the code: Current File is a native tree view (`vscode/currentFile.js`, `registerTreeDataProvider("imprimatur.currentFile", ...)`), with three groups — "Decisions and records" (ADRs and decisions ranked first), "Agent edits" and "Documented in" — newest first; a record opens with `imprimatur.records.reveal`, an edit with `imprimatur.openGraph`, a section with `imprimatur.app.open` (area "docs"); refreshed on `onDidChangeActiveTextEditor` and `onDidSaveTextDocument`.
